A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same ReNeg paper, with matching scientific text, equations, tables, and figures. Both end with references on page 10; neither supplied PDF contains the appendices mentioned in the text.

before.justification: v2 reports original ReNeg experiments, including benchmark comparisons, parameter-efficiency measurements, and image/video generation results in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–7.

after.justification: v3 retains the original ReNeg experimental results, including benchmark evaluations and transfer experiments with ControlNet, ZeroScope, and VideoCrafter2.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 retain the same reward-guided global embedding optimization, CFG training, DDIM sampling, and optional per-sample adaptation. Algorithm 1 is relocated but unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageReward prompts for training and evaluate on HPSv2 and Parti-Prompts. ControlNet image generation and ZeroScope/VideoCrafter2 video generation coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–5 and Figure 5. For example, TextCraftor (Text) remains in Table 2, and DPO-Diff remains in the qualitative comparison in Figure 5.

E3.justification: The reported protocols match, including dataset sizes, metrics, 4,000 global-training steps, 10 per-sample steps with patience 3, and 30-step DDIM inference at CFG 7.5 and 512 × 512 resolution.

E4.justification: The parameter-efficiency pilot, DDIM/DDPM prediction comparison, global/per-sample examples, and negative-embedding visualization remain unchanged in Table 1 and Figures 3, 4, and 6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run uncertainty summaries. Figure 5 retains the same statement about matching initial noise and seed for qualitative comparisons.

E6.justification: All numerical tables, plotted results, and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 2 retains Parti-Prompts HPSv2.1 scores of 29.16 for global embeddings and 29.84 for per-sample embeddings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the Jacobian-based parameter-efficiency definition, and the accompanying mathematical reasoning are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning reward-guided negative embeddings, human preference alignment, per-sample refinement, and transfer between models sharing a text encoder.

C2.justification: Interpretations of parameter efficiency, sampler behavior, and embedding visualizations are unchanged. The conclusion retains the limitation that the base model's generative ability can cause semantic deviations from prompts.

D1.justification: The optimizer, schedule, learning rate, batch size, and sampling details are identical. The code/embedding release statement and its link target are also unchanged; no additional implementation or resource details are supplied.

R1.justification: The same 41 works are cited, with unchanged positioning against prompt refinement and reward-based model finetuning. Changes to reference page pointers reflect pagination rather than citation additions or removals.

P1.justification: v3 adds author emails and explicit contribution, internship, correspondence, and project-lead notes, and revises affiliation/role markers. Scientific prose and section ordering remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded author block shifts Figure 1 and subsequent text flow. Algorithm 1 moves from page 5 to page 6, and the conclusion extends onto page 9. Figures and tables retain their content and visual designs.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies authorship and contact information and adjusts pagination. The methods, evidence, reproducibility details, claims, and limitations remain identical, so these limited editorial updates do not establish a meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
